name: DaVinci Bins Keywords And Smart Bins
use_when: A project has enough footage that manual browsing slows editing.
Documentary, event, tutorial, or multi-location footage needs searchable categories.
The agent needs reusable selects by topic, person, audio type, camera, or content.
avoid_when: The project has only a few clips and metadata work would slow the task.
The categories are speculative and will not affect edit decisions.
The footage is already organized by a reliable external logging system.

timeline_pattern.keyword_rule: Use keywords for categories the editor will search repeatedly.
timeline_pattern.smart_bin_rule: Smart bins should be live filters, not manual duplicate folders.
timeline_pattern.metadata_rule: Use list and metadata views when clip names alone are not enough.
timeline_pattern.fallback_rule: If Studio AI audio classification is unavailable, use manual keywords and smart bins.

motion.rule: Tag motion type or camera movement when movement continuity will matter later.

sound.rule: Tag clips by usable dialogue, ambience, music, SFX, noisy audio, or sync-needed status.

captions.rule: Tag clips that contain speech worth transcribing or captioning.

color.rule: Tag camera, scene, lighting condition, and log/profile when color matching will depend on source type.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use sidecar JSON/CSV metadata with clipId, keywords, camera, scene, audioQuality, transcriptStatus, and selected ranges.
implementation.remotion: Represent smart bins as filtered arrays over asset metadata.
implementation.blender: Use collection names and custom properties for footage categories when assembling mixed media scenes.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use folders/albums/favorites and filename prefixes when full metadata filters are unavailable.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use bins, labels, markers, metadata columns, search bins, and string-out selects.

common_mistakes: Logging everything with vague keywords that do not help edit decisions.
Creating manual duplicate bins when a live smart bin would stay current.
Relying on AI classification without checking whether it identified the useful content.
Waiting until the timeline is already crowded before tagging key footage.
qc: Can the editor find important people, scenes, audio, or topics without scrubbing every clip?
Do smart bins update when new matching media is tagged?
Are keyword names specific enough to drive edit choices?
Are AI-generated classifications checked before use?
Do metadata fields support audio sync, color matching, and story selects?
